chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Four rak'at after the Maghrib prayer, do not leave them, whether in residence or in travel.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing four rak'at after Maghrib prayer during travel?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the consistency of the four-rak'at voluntary prayer following Maghrib, explicitly extending its recommendation to both residents and travelers. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that certain *nawafil* (voluntary prayers) retain their status of high merit regardless of the changes in ritual brevity (*qasr*) that typically accompany travel. It serves as a reminder of the spiritual continuity required in daily devotion, transcending the physical circumstances of one's journey or home.
